verdict.rationale: Mollie documents two scope-reduction paths: Mollie Components (Mollie JS), which add card-holder data fields to your own checkout in a way described as "fully PCI-DSS SAQ-A compliant", and hosted Mollie Checkout pages where the customer completes payment on Mollie's side. SAQ-A eligibility implies card data stays off the merchant's servers, but the pack never explicitly describes tokenization or states that card data bypasses merchant systems. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the card tokenization mechanism, an explicit statement that raw card data never reaches merchant servers, independent or hands-on corroboration of the SAQ-A scope reduction.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my systems out of most of PCI DSS scope because card data is tokenized and never touches my servers

citations.quote: Mollie JS is a set of Javascript APIs that allow you to add the fields needed for credit card holder data to your own checkout, in a way that is fully PCI-DSS SAQ-A compliant.
Mollie Components (embeddable card components for PCI scope reduction)
These hosted payment pages allow your customer to select their payment method of choice and to complete the payment.
